## 🔒 Claimed — `domain:ui` seat

- **Session**: `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`
- **Branch**: `claude/issue-6875-grid-relational-meta-derive`
- **Seat post**: objectstack-ai/objectui#5560

All agents share one GitHub identity, so the assignee field cannot tell you whose claim this is — this comment (session ID + branch) is the claim. Different session ID reading this? It's taken.

**No collision.** `plugin-grid` and `plugin-dashboard` are untouched by the five things in flight (`plugin-charts`, `plugin-detail/ActivityTimeline`, `components/__tests__`, `components/custom/view-states` + `plugin-list/ListView`, `app-shell/views/studio-design`).

**Dispatched with the card's own first step as the gating measurement**, not as a footnote: *"Whether the object schema a live `getObjectSchema` returns ever carries the camelCase spellings […] decides how much of item 2 is reachable today, and it is the first thing triage should run."* If the server normalises on the way out, a large part of this card is unreachable and it shrinks — **that is a legitimate result**, and I would rather have it measured than have an agent widen an alias list to fix something nothing can produce.

**Direction stays open, with one fence.** The card is right that contract-first may put the answer at the producer rather than in a hand-kept alias list (AGENTS.md #0.1 — a tolerant renderer fossilises a second dialect). ⛔ But if the chosen direction would widen a published type or public export, that engages Clause ② and needs `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` — which the exhausted fable quota currently blocks. Stop and report rather than route around it.

The card's structural instruction is carried as a ruling: **derive the copy set from the consumers' read set, do not restate it.** A hand-maintained list is what drifted here; a hand-maintained list is not the fix.

## 🟢 Landed — `9700dd94e`

PR objectstack-ai/objectui#7156 merged; `main` advanced. `Fixes` closed this card.

### Verified by content — and my first control returned zero

| probe | pre (`85b5077d7`) | post (`9700dd94e`) |
|---|---|---|
| `plugin-grid/src/relationalMetaKeys.ts` exists | **0** | **1** |
| `displayField` / `descriptionField` / `lookupColumns` in it | — | **4 / 3 / 3** |
| ⚠️ CONTROL `RELATIONAL_META_KEYS` in `ObjectGrid.tsx` | 2 | **0** |

My planned control **came back zero**, which by this seat's own rule is no control at all. Re-taken against live symbols in the same file: `applyRelationalMeta` = **5**, `fieldMeta` = **40**, and `relationalMetaKeys` imported **2×**. So `ObjectGrid.tsx` reads fine — the constant genuinely **moved out** into the new module, which is the change, not a broken probe. A zero I could not distinguish from a dead instrument until I put a working one beside it.

And the thing I ruled for is on `main`: `relationalMetaCopySet.derivation.test.ts` — the gate that re-extracts the read set from the consumer sources.

### The gating measurement came back opposite, and the card grew

I made the card's own first step a ruling: *does a live `getObjectSchema` ever emit the camelCase spellings?* The card framed "no" as shrinking the work. It inverted:

- `FieldSchema` is **strict**, 71 props (the card said 64), declaring camelCase and **none** of the snake twins — `reference_field` parses to `unrecognized_keys`.
- objectstack emits **zero** snake_case (`display_field` 3 files against a `displayField` control of 68).
- `getObjectSchema` rewrites **only** the `reference`/`reference_to` pair.

⇒ **camelCase is the only dialect a live path can carry, and it was exactly the half the grid never copied.**

### The bug was shown, not asserted

Two columns over one data source and one referenced record, differing **only in spelling**: the control resolved `ACME-42`, the spec-spelled column resolved `Wrong Name` — `1 failed | 1 passed (2)` on the unmodified tree, both correct after. That is the difference between "the key isn't copied" (a code fact) and "the cell shows the wrong thing" (the bug).

### The producer-side branch was rejected on the merits

I fenced against taking the cheap direction and calling it the design conclusion. The internal fix was not taken because it was affordable — the producer fix was rejected because extending `normalizeFieldReferenceKeys` would stamp `display_field` **from** `displayField`, **manufacturing the dialect the contract refuses**. AGENTS.md §0.1 running backwards.

Three of five keys added; two deliberately **not** — `FieldSchema` declares neither, so no producer can fill them, and the gate proves that absence rather than asserting it.

### Follow-ups

**objectui#7154** — four more spec-declared keys (`multiple`, `allowCreate`, `lookupPageSize`, `dependsOn`) read on this path and never copied, found *by the derivation itself*. **Now unblocked.** Kept out of this PR on my ruling: each changes picker behaviour and deserves the rendering proof `displayField` got, and the derivation carries them as `deferred` so the gate keeps them visible — which is what makes deferring safe rather than merely cautious.

**objectui#7155** — `needs-user-decision`. The consumer chains read the snake spelling **first**, so retiring a leg changes which value *wins*, not merely which keys exist; and hosts outside these two repos are invisible to any measurement available here. A back-compat call, correctly filed rather than acted on.

## ⚠️ CORRECTION to my landing note — two of the three keys this card shipped are INERT

objectui#7154's implementer measured the seam properly and the result reaches back into this card. Recording it here because my landing note above praised *"three of five keys added"* and that framing was too generous.

### The mechanism I did not check

`applyRelationalMeta` writes onto the `fieldMeta` handed to **`CellRenderer`** — the read-only cell. But the **inline editor is a different seam**: `renderCellEditor` looks the field up in `objectSchema` and **spreads the whole def** into the widget, so every key a def carries reaches `LookupField` *regardless of the copy set*.

Both halves read `objectSchema.fields[name]`. So copying a key onto the bag could never rescue an editor the schema read already served.

⇒ Of the three keys this card added:

| key | read by | genuinely delivered? |
|---|---|---|
| `displayField` | `LookupCellRenderer` — **reads the bag** | ✅ **yes**, and the rendering test proves it |
| `descriptionField` | `LookupField` — reached via the **schema spread** | ❌ inert on this bag |
| `lookupColumns` | `LookupField` — same | ❌ inert on this bag |

**This card delivered 1 of the 3 keys it shipped.** The `displayField` half is real and stays pinned — and notably, it is real *precisely because* it was the one backed by a rendering test showing `ACME-42` vs `Wrong Name`. The two inert keys had no such test; they were classified from a read-set derivation, which establishes that a *consumer reads the key* and not that *this bag is how it arrives*.

### What that says about the evidence bar

The bar held exactly where it was applied and failed exactly where it was not. I required rendering evidence for the defect and got it — for one key. I accepted derivation alone for the other two, and derivation cannot distinguish "a consumer reads this key" from "this path is how the consumer gets it."

Filed as **objectui#7166**: 6 of the 10 keys `ObjectGrid` copies onto a column's `fieldMeta` have no reader on that bag, two of them added here. That is the objectui#6711 / objectui#6874 class, arriving from the other direction.

### What is NOT undermined

- The **gating measurement** stands: the spec is strict, declares only camelCase, and objectstack emits no snake_case.
- The **derivation and its gate** stand and are the durable win — objectui#7154 used them to find this.
- The **user-visible bug** stands: `displayField` genuinely fixed a lookup cell rendering the wrong value.
- The **producer-side rejection** stands on its own merits.

The card is not reopened — its defect is fixed and pinned. The over-delivery is recorded here and carried as objectui#7166.
